outcome: Since 26 January 2024 one preprint bears on this problem: Roy and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv:2605.25733, posted 25 May 2026) claim a complete forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of word-representable near-triangulations, which would cover the K4-containing case, but the general proof is only a sketch in the text I could read, no human engagement or citing work was found about four and a half months on, and the paper's new seven-vertex graph conflicts with the seven-vertex list it cites.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the Wikipedia bullet. (1) The class: planar near-triangulations, meaning planar graphs in which every bounded (inner) face is a triangle, with the outer face unrestricted. (2) The subclass: those containing K4. The bullet says containing the complete graph K4; Glen (2016) states the open problem as K4 as an induced subgraph, and this record reads it that way. (3) The task: characterise which of these are word-representable, in any form (the bullet fixes no form, such as forbidden induced subgraphs or structure). The bullet's parenthetical says a characterisation is already known for K4-free planar graphs; that is context, not part of the ask. Scope note: Glen's own statement of the open problem is wider, covering near-triangulations and graphs in general that contain K4 as an induced subgraph; the bullet confines it to near-triangulations, so only that is asked here. A sibling bullet asks to characterise (non-)word-representable planar graphs in general; it is not asked here.

events.what_happened: Marc Elliot Glen, 'Colourability and word-representability of near-triangulations', arXiv:1605.01688 (v1 5 May 2016; later versions 20 May 2016, 20 Oct 2016, 28 Sep 2018). Proves that a near-triangulation with no K4 as an induced subgraph is word-representable iff it is 3-colourable (Theorem 2 as rendered), and gives a shorter proof of the Diks, Kowalik and Kurowski internal-evenness criterion for 3-colourability. States that the classification of near-triangulations, and of graphs in general, that contain K4 as an induced subgraph 'is still left as an open problem', and claims to solve all open problems of Glen and Kitaev (2015). Its Corollary 1, as rendered in the ar5iv HTML I read, says a K4-free near-triangulation is word-representable iff it is perfect. Published as Pure Mathematics and Applications (PU.M.A.) 28(1), pp. 70–76, submitted 28 Sep 2018, accepted 9 Sep 2019, online 1 Nov 2019 (DOI 10.1515/puma-2015-0032). I did not check whether v1 already contained Corollary 1.
events.revisions: v1 5 May 2016; v2 20 May 2016; v3 20 Oct 2016; v4 28 Sep 2018 (the version the arXiv abs page lists as current); journal version PU.M.A. 2019.
events.delivers: For near-triangulations with no K4 as an induced subgraph only: word-representable iff 3-colourable (equivalently, internally even). Corollary 1 as rendered adds: for K4-free near-triangulations, word-representable iff perfect. That corollary is the claim the 2026 preprint says is wrong. Nothing about near-triangulations containing K4.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The K4-containing near-triangulations are explicitly left open by this paper.

events.time_since_posted: Posted May 2016 and published November 2019. The Corollary 1 error was first stated publicly on 25 May 2026 in the Roy and Hariharasubramanian preprint, about ten years after arXiv v1.
events.directly_checkable: The K4-free counterexample to Corollary 1 is a small finite graph (Figure 2 of arXiv:2605.25733). I did not check it.
events.doubts: Corollary 1 (K4-free: word-representable iff perfect) is contradicted by a K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable near-triangulation, which is therefore word-representable. The 2026 preprint presents this as Figure 2 and says it rectifies the claim. I did not verify the counterexample myself. The main K4-free theorem (3-colourable iff word-representable) is not disputed; the 2026 preprint uses it.
events.direction: Does not touch the K4-containing case, which it leaves open. For the neighbouring K4-free case it proves the 3-colourability equivalence and asserts a perfection equivalence that the 2026 preprint says is false.

events.what_happened: Prosper Akrobotu, Sergey Kitaev, Zuzana Masárová, 'On word-representability of polyomino triangulations', arXiv:1405.3527 (posted 14 May 2014). Shows that a triangulation of any convex polyomino is word-representable iff 3-colourable; shows this fails for arbitrary polyominoes; shows that replacing each 4-cycle of a polyomino by K4 gives a word-representable graph. The 2026 preprint's reference list gives the journal as Siberian Advances in Mathematics 25(1) (2015), pp. 1–10; I did not check that.
events.revisions: Single version (v1), per the arXiv abs page.
events.delivers: Triangulations of convex polyominoes: word-representable iff 3-colourable. A separate K4 statement about polyominoes with 4-cycles replaced by K4. This is a polyomino class, not near-triangulations in general (Glen 2016 says near-triangulations generalise it).
events.remains: All of problem_asks. This is a neighbouring class with no K4-containing near-triangulation content that I could see.

Glen (2016) says this class is generalised by near-triangulations and that the open problems stated here are solved there.

events.what_happened: Thomas Z.Q. Chen, Sergey Kitaev, Brian Y. Sun, 'Word-representability of triangulations of grid-covered cylinder graphs', arXiv:1507.06749 (v1 24 Jul 2015; v2 27 Jul 2015). The 2026 preprint lists this among the subclasses it says it unifies. K4 is not mentioned in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Suchanda Roy and Ramesh Hariharasubramanian (Department of Mathematics, IIT Guwahati), 'Characterization of Word-Representable Near-Triangulations', arXiv:2605.25733 (math.CO, cross-listed cs.DM), v1 posted 25 May 2026. No later version is listed on the abstract page I read. Claims: (i) Theorem 16: a near-triangulation G is word-representable iff it contains none of the graphs of Figure 8 as an induced subgraph, presented as a complete characterisation by forbidden induced subgraphs. (ii) Theorem 15: a K4-free near-triangulation is word-representable iff it is odd-wheel-free (contains no induced W_{2k+1}), derived from the 3-colourability criterion and the paper's Theorem 7. (iii) It corrects Glen's Corollary 1 (K4-free: word-representable iff perfect) with a K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable, hence word-representable, near-triangulation (Figure 2). (iv) It identifies a new minimal non-word-representable graph on seven vertices, A″ (Figure 8), which it says does not appear among the 25 seven-vertex minimal non-word-representable graphs listed by Kitaev et al. (its reference [13], Kitaev and Sun 2024). Section 3 contains Lemma 3.1 (type-1 near-triangulation with outer face of length 3: word-representable iff odd-wheel-free), Lemma 3.2 (type-3 near-triangulation with outer face of length 3: not word-representable) and Remark 2 (outer face of length at most 3: word-representable iff locally comparability and free of F1, A, A′, A″, A‴). The proof of Theorem 16 is headed 'Sketch of the proof' and runs by induction on outer-face length; the base cases (lengths 4 and 5) are asserted rather than shown in the text I could read.
events.revisions: v1 25 May 2026 only, as far as the abstract page shows when read on 11 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Claims, for the whole class of near-triangulations and therefore for those containing K4, a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of word-representability (Theorem 16). The forbidden family in Figure 8 includes an infinite odd-wheel family W_{2k+1} (k>1) and finitely many named graphs (A, A′, A″, A‴, B, B′, B″, C, C′, D–H, F1–F3, as labelled in the text). Support I could read: the outer-face-length-3 case (Lemmas 3.1, 3.2, Remark 2). The outer-face-length-4-and-above step is a sketch in the text read. Restrictions: near-triangulations only, the bullet's class; the paper says nothing about graphs in general containing K4.
events.remains: If Theorem 16 holds, nothing of problem_asks remains. If its sketched induction does not hold, the K4-containing case with outer face length at least 4 remains open. Not addressed: graphs in general containing K4 (Glen's broader wording). Its concluding remarks point to planar word-representability in general, a sibling bullet, as still needing work.
events.time_since_posted: About 4.5 months (25 May to 11 Oct 2026). No review, comment, citing paper or journal decision found.
events.directly_checkable: The forbidden graphs and the Figure 2 counterexample are finite and small. Word-representability can be checked by searching for a semi-transitive orientation, so each could be checked by hand or by computer. I did not check any of them, because the figures were not readable to me.
events.doubts: (a) Theorem 16 is proved only by a sketch: induction on outer-face length with base cases asserted, as the text reads. (b) Conflict with the earlier seven-vertex list. The paper says A″ is missing from the 25 listed by Kitaev et al. Kitaev and Sun (RAIRO-ITA 58 (2024), article 9; arXiv:2110.05405) caption their Figure 3 'All non-word-representable graphs on 7 vertices'. If A″ is minimal and non-word-representable, that list is incomplete; if it is not, A″ is misdescribed. I could not read Figure 3 or A″ and so cannot tell which. (c) The paper says it corrects 'two inaccuracies in earlier papers [7, 13]' but states only the [7] one (Corollary 1). The [13] inaccuracy is not specified. (d) Single arXiv preprint; no journal, referee or erratum record found. (e) The quotes above come from a summarising fetch of the HTML rendering, not from verbatim reading, and I could not check them against the text.
events.direction: Cuts toward answering the bullet, not against any conjecture: it claims the characterisation the bullet asks for, in forbidden-induced-subgraph form. It also contradicts Glen's K4-free perfect corollary, and its A″ claim appears to disagree with the seven-vertex list of Kitaev and Sun. Whether it settles the K4-containing case depends on the proof of Theorem 16.
events.object: Two explicit small graphs, shown in figures I could not read. (1) A K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable near-triangulation (Figure 2). It is word-representable, so it refutes the 'iff perfect' claim. (2) A″ (Figure 8), described as a new minimal non-word-representable graph on seven vertices. The text I read gives no further construction for either. Both are finite and explicit as far as the text shows, not existence proofs.

disputes.summary: Roy and Hariharasubramanian say Glen's Corollary 1 (a K4-free near-triangulation is word-representable iff perfect) is wrong, and give a K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable counterexample. Glen's journal version was accepted in 2019 and the claim was not withdrawn; it is superseded only by the 2026 preprint. The 2026 preprint also says it corrects 'two inaccuracies' in [7] and [13] but names only the [7] one.

The 2026 preprint says its new seven-vertex minimal non-word-representable graph A″ is not among the 25 seven-vertex graphs in the list of Kitaev et al. (cited as Kitaev and Sun 2024), whose Figure 3 is captioned 'All non-word-representable graphs on 7 vertices'. Both cannot be right as stated; I could not read the figures to decide which is wrong.

summary: One post-window event bears on the bullet. Roy and Hariharasubramanian (arXiv:2605.25733, v1 25 May 2026, no later version on the abstract page read) claim a complete characterisation of word-representable near-triangulations by forbidden induced subgraphs (Theorem 16: word-representable iff no induced subgraph from Figure 8), which would cover the K4-containing case. They also state Theorem 15 (a K4-free near-triangulation is word-representable iff odd-wheel-free) and correct Glen's 2016 Corollary 1 (K4-free: word-representable iff perfect) with a K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable counterexample. I read the paper only through the arXiv HTML rendering, via a summarising fetch; the PDF text was not decodable. In that reading, Section 3 settles outer-face-length-3 cases (Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2, Remark 2), while the general Theorem 16 is labelled 'Sketch of the proof', an induction on outer-face length whose base cases are asserted. The paper's new seven-vertex graph A″ is said not to appear among the 25 seven-vertex minimal non-word-representable graphs of Kitaev and Sun (2024), whose Figure 3 is captioned as the complete list. I could read neither figure, so this conflict is unresolved: either A″ is misdescribed or the Kitaev–Sun list is incomplete. Close call on whether this settles the problem: the reading that it does rests on Theorem 16 as claimed and the length-3 lemmas; the reading that it does not rests on the sketch-level general proof and the A″ conflict. Silence: I found no review, comment, citing paper, journal decision, or erratum for the 2026 preprint in 36 searches. The Wikipedia article on word-representable graphs (last edited 9 Aug 2026) still lists the K4 bullet as open, but that is an encyclopedia, not an expert source. Glen's 2016 arXiv paper (K4-free case; K4 case explicitly open) was published in PU.M.A. in 2019, and the K4-free perfect corollary I read in its ar5iv rendering was not caught there; the preprint says that corollary is wrong. Neighbouring pre-2024 subclass results (Akrobotu et al. 2014; Glen and Kitaev 2015; Chen, Kitaev and Sun 2015) concern polyomino and grid-cylinder triangulations and do not mention K4-containing near-triangulations. An unread 2025 Lehigh thesis by Hauser on chordal near-triangulations is known only from a citation and may bear on the K4 case. AI involvement: the AI search (problem name with AI, LLM, GPT, Claude, Erdős and tracker terms) found no AI system credited with any word-representability result. The 2026 preprint's readable headings (Abstract, Introduction, Preliminaries, Characterization, Concluding Remarks, References) contain no acknowledgements, funding, declarations or AI statement, though I read this only through the summarising fetch. The AI-linked items I opened (the kingy.ai Petersen counterexample record, whose AI role is GPT-5.6 Sol assistance with presentation, and the Sra 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' preprint, arXiv:2608.29595) do not mention word-representability, colouring or near-triangulations. The kingy.ai tracker index was not searched directly.
competing_reading: The 2026 preprint has not settled the bullet. Its Theorem 16 is proved only by a sketch for outer faces of length 4 and above, the rigorous-looking lemmas cover only outer faces of length 3, and its A″ graph contradicts the completeness claim of the seven-vertex list it builds on. On this reading the K4-containing case stays open, with partial progress: the length-3 case and the K4-free case (odd-wheel-free). Glen's wider open problem (graphs in general containing K4) is untouched by any reading.
what_would_settle_it: A verbatim reading of arXiv:2605.25733 (its PDF or TeX source): the full proof of Theorem 16 and of Lemmas 3.1–3.2; Figure 2 and Figure 8, including the construction of A″ and whether it is minimal and non-word-representable. Then check A″ against Figure 3 of Kitaev and Sun (2024), or by computer, since a semi-transitive orientation search on a seven-vertex graph is cheap. Also needed: the Hauser (2025) thesis, to see whether its chordal results cover K4-containing cases; a referee report or journal decision on the 2026 preprint; and any citing paper that reproduces or refutes Theorem 16.

Not addressed: graphs in general containing K4 (Glen's broader wording). Its concluding remarks point to planar word-representability in general, a sibling bullet, as still needing work.
event.time_since_posted: About 4.5 months (25 May to 11 Oct 2026). No review, comment, citing paper or journal decision found.
event.directly_checkable: The forbidden graphs and the Figure 2 counterexample are finite and small. Word-representability can be checked by searching for a semi-transitive orientation, so each could be checked by hand or by computer. I did not check any of them, because the figures were not readable to me.
event.doubts: (a) Theorem 16 is proved only by a sketch: induction on outer-face length with base cases asserted, as the text reads. (b) Conflict with the earlier seven-vertex list. The paper says A″ is missing from the 25 listed by Kitaev et al. Kitaev and Sun (RAIRO-ITA 58 (2024), article 9; arXiv:2110.05405) caption their Figure 3 'All non-word-representable graphs on 7 vertices'. If A″ is minimal and non-word-representable, that list is incomplete; if it is not, A″ is misdescribed. I could not read Figure 3 or A″ and so cannot tell which. (c) The paper says it corrects 'two inaccuracies in earlier papers [7, 13]' but states only the [7] one (Corollary 1). The [13] inaccuracy is not specified. (d) Single arXiv preprint; no journal, referee or erratum record found. (e) The quotes above come from a summarising fetch of the HTML rendering, not from verbatim reading, and I could not check them against the text.
event.direction: Cuts toward answering the bullet, not against any conjecture: it claims the characterisation the bullet asks for, in forbidden-induced-subgraph form. It also contradicts Glen's K4-free perfect corollary, and its A″ claim appears to disagree with the seven-vertex list of Kitaev and Sun. Whether it settles the K4-containing case depends on the proof of Theorem 16.
event.object: Two explicit small graphs, shown in figures I could not read. (1) A K4-free, non-perfect, 3-colourable near-triangulation (Figure 2). It is word-representable, so it refutes the 'iff perfect' claim. (2) A″ (Figure 8), described as a new minimal non-word-representable graph on seven vertices. The text I read gives no further construction for either. Both are finite and explicit as far as the text shows, not existence proofs.

events.credibility_reason: Main K4-free theorem undisputed, but Corollary 1 (K4-free: word-representable iff perfect) is contradicted by a counterexample in the 2026 preprint.
Known only from a citation; content unread, so nothing it settles can be established.

General Theorem 16 is proved only by a 'sketch' with base cases asserted; its new seven-vertex graph A″ conflicts with the Kitaev–Sun list it cites as complete; one of two claimed corrections is unspecified; no uptake after ~4.5 months. Authors work in the area and no specific error in a key step is identified, so not set aside.

judgement.why: The statement asks only about near-triangulations containing K4; the K4-free case is named as already known context, so Glen 2016 (K4-free) and the polyomino/cylinder subclass papers do not settle any restriction of the K4-containing question and are answered variant. The Roy–Hariharasubramanian preprint claims a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation of all near-triangulations, which on the statement's wording answers the whole ask; scope is whole, verification unreviewed (no engagement found; finite forbidden graphs are checkable individually but the characterisation itself is not directly checkable). The close call was credibility: the sketch-level induction and the A″ conflict are real doubts but not a specific unanswered error, and the authors are in-field, so doubtful rather than not_credible or knocked_down. Its direction is 'confirmed' in the sense of answering the asked characterisation; its exhibited graphs (Figure 2 counterexample to Glen's corollary, A″) do not bear on the statement as witness or counterexample. The Hauser thesis is year-only 2025, hence after the snapshot, but unread, so scope none.
judgement.doubts: Roy–Hariharasubramanian content was read only through a summarising fetch of the HTML; theorem statements, the 'sketch' label and the absence of AI acknowledgements rest on that. Hauser's thesis on chordal near-triangulations may contain a genuine case result on K4-containing graphs, but the record cannot show it. Glen-Kitaev 2015 journal publication unverified, hence unreviewed.
